author: Mary Macaulay
text: Check the reading on your Libre about 15 minutes after your finger stick. Fingerstick uses blood and sensor uses interstitial fluid. They won’t match exactly. Each instrument can be off 20% either way. Your readings are within a normal range of each other. Also, I put my new sensor on my arm 1 day before the old sensor finishes. It gives the new sensor adjustment time. I start the new one right after the old one is done.

author: Steve Kuckuk
text: It can (may) take over 24 hours (24 - 48) for the sensor to 'settle in' (reduce inflammation from knife blade's inserting the sensor’s filament) and give stabile readings . . . 'For me', I put the new sensor on my skin a full day ahead of needing it and then activate the new sensor a day later when the old one expires . . . The 14/15 days of usefulness counter will not begin until activation . . .
